question: Which of the following is a Buddhist temple in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabodhi Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mahabodhi Temple** is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, India.
 
• This temple marks the location where Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, is said to have attained enlightenment under the Bodhi Tree.
 
• The current structure of the Mahabodhi Temple was built during the Gupta period in the 5th-6th century CE.
 
• It is one of the earliest Buddhist temples built entirely of brick and considered one of the most significant shrines in Buddhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**

 
 
• There are 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India, including cultural, natural, and mixed properties.
 
• These sites are recognized for their exceptional cultural or natural importance to the common heritage of humanity.
 
 
 
• **Buddhism in India:**
 
 
• Buddhism originated in India around the 5th century BCE with Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha.
 
• Key Buddhist pilgrimage sites in India include Lumbini (birthplace of Buddha), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment), Sarnath (first sermon), and Kushinagar (death).
 
 
 
• **Other Significant Buddhist Temples in India:**
 
 
• Mahaparinirvana Temple in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh
 
• Dhamek Stupa in Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh
 
• Ramabhar Stupa in Kushinagar, Uttar Pradesh
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Mahabodhi Temple:**
 
 
• The temple complex includes a large central tower, standing 55 meters tall, surrounded by four smaller towers.
